json.reason: JS API misuse: Array.prototype.sort() with no comparator compares elements as strings, which silently mis-orders numeric arrays; the bug is syntactically detectable as a zero-argument .sort() in a numeric context.
json.title: Numeric array sorted with .sort() and no comparator
json.message: .sort() without a comparator compares numbers as strings (e.g. [10, 9, 100] -> [10, 100, 9]); pass (a, b) => a - b.
json.note: Array.prototype.sort() coerces elements to strings and compares them lexicographically, so arrays of numbers come out in the wrong order. In a function whose result type is numeric, always pass an explicit numeric comparator such as (a, b) => a - b (default sorting is fine only for strings).
json.rule_yaml:
rule:
  kind: call_expression
  all:
    - pattern: $ARR.sort()
    - inside:
        stopBy: end
        has:
          field: return_type
          regex: "number"
